title: How the Work Becomes Cash: Procurement, Delivery and Working Capital

web_blocks.text: RNIT sells software development, AI design, digital platforms, consulting, support and maintenance. The audited revenue policy describes time-and-material, fixed-price, milestone, subscription and managed-service arrangements. These formats distribute delivery and collection risk differently. FY2026’s auditor made revenue recognition a key audit matter, citing performance obligations, percentage-of-completion estimates, unbilled contract assets and customer acceptance. You should treat award, recognized revenue, acceptance, invoice and cash as separate stages. A signed scope establishes opportunity, not collected economics. [1]

Public-sector opportunities are visible through named notices. APSSDC’s NIA announcement and the Higher Education agreement identify customers and defined scopes including design, development, integration, deployment and maintenance. The notices establish public-sector engagements, but not every bid step, channel structure, reseller role, procurement conversion or renewal. The annual report does not disclose bid pipeline, commissions or system-integrator dependence. Describe the route only where filings support it: a named public buyer, a specified software program and implementation obligations. [5] [6]

Current filed pricing examples are more specific than a generic SaaS label. The executed Andhra Pradesh Higher Education SLA charges by attendance authentication over a two-year agreement; Telangana’s FRS rate contracts operate under a SaaS model but do not publish a per-user tariff. The 22 September 2026 APSSDC NIA award bills per minute per user, ties payment to actual usage and satisfactory delivery, provides a five-year services term from signing, and is classified by RNIT as Tier 7 (above ₹25 crore inclusive of GST). The tier is a company classification, not guaranteed cash; actual interviews, acceptance and invoicing determine the outcome. [6] [11] [43] A November 2025 Telangana Social Welfare filing similarly described usage-based SaaS consideration for attendance across 268 institutions; it did not disclose the tariff. [44]

Delivery can blend RNIT’s own work with outside components. The accounting policy says integrated contracts may contain subcontractor services and third-party equipment or software. RNIT assesses whether it controls goods or services before transfer; acting as agent means reporting revenue net, acting as principal means reporting gross. This distinction can affect growth and margins even when underlying project value is similar. The reports do not name vendors, hardware sources, hosting providers or supply-chain concentrations. Do not assume all recognized revenue represents a proprietary software license. [1]

Acceptance is a cash gate. Fixed-price maintenance can be recognized ratably or by percentage of completion depending on the service pattern; other fixed-price contracts use effort or cost incurred relative to estimates. The auditor says it tested contracts, timesheets, milestone confirmations, customer acceptance and unbilled revenue. That is not an adverse finding; it maps the judgments. Monitor contract-asset ageing, billing milestones, customer sign-off and post-period collections. Deployment that is active but not accepted may delay billing or change revenue timing. [1]

Management says SaaS and operations-and-maintenance revenue supported FY2025, and the audited policy recognizes subscription and managed-service contracts. Yet there is no SaaS revenue share, contract-duration profile or recurring-revenue reconciliation. Do not assume every customer pays by user, month or usage event. Public programs may be milestone or fixed-price arrangements; a cloud product could bill differently. The source does not provide tariffs. Track subscription revenue and renewals only when reported, and avoid turning “SaaS” into a claim that the majority of revenue is recurring. [1] [2]

This waterfall converts audited FY2026 lakh figures to crore by dividing by 100. Per ₹100 of operating revenue, employee cost is about ₹15.44, combined consultancy and other operating costs ₹44.40, D&A ₹7.77, interest ₹1.65, other income adds ₹1.52, and tax is ₹8.92. PAT is roughly ₹23.34. CFO is about ₹21.81, while fixed-asset and intangible purchases are ₹36.83; CFO less capex is negative ₹15.02 per ₹100 revenue. This is a deterministic bridge, not a forecast. `other_opex` combines ₹1,460.27 lakh operating consultancy expense with ₹826.22 lakh other expenses so the bridge reconciles to the audited income statement. [1]

FY2026 CFO needs a quality check. The cash-flow statement includes an increase in borrowings of ₹983.46 lakh and increase in current tax liabilities of ₹418.04 lakh among operating adjustments. Receivables absorbed ₹628.62 lakh, loans and advances ₹291.12 lakh and other current assets ₹616.85 lakh. The investing section shows ₹1,896.75 lakh of fixed/intangible purchases and ₹1,810.94 lakh placed in other financial assets. Report CFO as filed, but do not imply it is all customer cash collected. [1]

H1 FY2027 is a separate unaudited observation: revenue ₹2,425.85 lakh and PAT ₹550.92 lakh accompanied negative CFO of ₹710.32 lakh. The half-year cash-flow statement records a ₹1,021.21 lakh increase in receivables and ₹617.19 lakh increase in other current assets. At September, receivables were ₹3,084.54 lakh, cash ₹468.72 lakh versus ₹2,867.86 lakh at March, and total current plus non-current borrowings had increased. These lines explain the negative operating cash result; they do not alone prove bad debt. Do not mix half-year income with annual cash flow. [3]

Data governance and security are operating requirements. Identity, education and welfare workflows may handle personal data; conversational AI may handle user inputs. The permitted reports do not specify RNIT’s data-fiduciary or processor role by deployment, hosting location, retention schedule, access model, deletion controls or breach history. The FY2025 letter commits to responsible AI, transparency and security, while FY2026 lists cybersecurity and data protection as risks. Do not infer that a public customer bears every obligation or that policy language proves operational controls. [1] [2]

A commercial diligence sequence is award, contracting, design, integration, deployment, test, customer acceptance, invoice, collection and renewal. RNIT’s filings establish specific engagements and disclose policies for time-based and milestone revenue, but do not publish project conversion rates or lag times. A system may be technically launched while acceptance or final billing remains outstanding. The FY2026 auditor says it reviewed scopes, timesheets, milestone confirmations and customer acceptance. Future disclosure of award-to-signoff days and unbilled balances would make delivery quality easier to judge. [1] [5] [6]

The audited FY2026 income statement reconciles to the ₹100 bridge. Revenue ₹5,149.88 lakh less employee expense ₹795.29 lakh and combined operating/other expense ₹2,286.49 lakh, plus other income ₹78.03 lakh, less D&A ₹400.16 lakh, finance cost ₹84.95 lakh and tax ₹459.29 lakh yields PAT ₹1,201.73 lakh. Each lakh amount was divided by 100 for crore. The bridge block uses annual audited figures only, not half-year or TTM data. CFO ₹1,123.15 lakh less capex and intangible purchases ₹1,896.75 lakh leaves negative ₹773.60 lakh after investment. [1]

The reported FY2026 CFO was positive, but its reconciliation deserves a note. The operating section includes ₹983.46 lakh from an increase in borrowings and ₹418.04 lakh from current tax liabilities, while receivables, loans and advances and other current assets absorbed cash. Report the filed CFO rather than implying an accounting error; the point is that CFO is not identical to customer receipts. A direct bank-receipts bridge and clearer separation of operating from financing movements would improve cash-quality analysis. The waterfall retains the company’s audited CFO because it is the required deterministic base. [1]

H1 FY2027 is a useful but limited stress test. The interim statement is unaudited and covers six months; operating cash flow was negative ₹710.32 lakh. Receivables increased by ₹1,021.21 lakh and other current assets by ₹617.19 lakh in the half-year cash-flow statement. At September, receivables were ₹3,084.54 lakh, other current assets ₹2,248.82 lakh and cash ₹468.72 lakh. Capital work in progress was ₹1,482.93 lakh. These movements may reflect contract growth or collection delays; subsequent receipts and acceptance will distinguish the explanations. [3]

Supply-chain disclosure is limited. RNIT’s accounting policy recognizes that integrated service arrangements can use subcontractors and third-party software or equipment, and it assesses whether it acts as principal or agent. The reports do not name hosting partners, biometric hardware suppliers, model providers or vendor concentration. This may involve less inventory exposure than manufacturing, but critical service dependencies remain. Ask whether components have alternatives, how vendor security is reviewed and whether customer data passes through subprocessors. Do not invent a hardware bill of materials or assume every layer is built in-house. [1]

The data-security path also deserves separate diligence. Identity and education systems may connect mobile devices, biometric records, student databases, departmental APIs and cloud or on-premise hosting. A vulnerability can affect users and the customer, not just vendor margins. RNIT cites cybersecurity and data protection as risks and management commits to responsible AI, but the permitted filings do not provide deployment-level architecture, retention schedules, certifications, incidents or deletion controls. The stronger the mission-critical claim, the more useful independent security evidence becomes. [1] [2]

Working capital connects delivery to financing. FY2026 year-end included trade receivables of ₹2,063.34 lakh, contract assets of ₹515 lakh, supplier advances of ₹558.03 lakh, expense advances of ₹177.88 lakh and other current assets of ₹1,631.63 lakh. These are not all overdue customer invoices; they include different operational balances. H1 FY2027 shows receivables and other current assets increasing while cash falls. Separate receivables from advances, taxes and guarantees, and then trace which balances unwind through collection or completed work. That is more precise than calling all current-asset growth a collection problem. [1] [3]

The support phase matters after acceptance. Maintenance may be recognized over time, but its value depends on service levels, renewal and cost-to-serve. A long government relationship can create stable work while still requiring a fresh extension or budget approval. The reports do not disclose support renewal cohorts, so do not equate maintenance language with automatic recurring cash. [1] [2]

Three delivery routes show the range of working-capital exposure. The AP FRS SLA combines integration, training, maintenance and transaction pricing; the TGTS work orders use a three-year SaaS rate-contract model; APSSDC’s NIA award depends on per-minute usage and acceptance. The 2026 CCE module award carries two months of development and five years of O&M, while the OMCAP platform notice specifies 90 working days. Contract duration does not equal collected revenue: confirm signing, implementation, user activation, sign-off, invoicing and post-period cash for each scope. [6] [11] [13] [43]

epigraph.quote: The Company’s business model—anchored in SaaS-based and milestone-linked billings, complemented by long-term partnerships with government departments—continues to provide stability and clear forward visibility.
epigraph.author: Raja Srinivas Nandigam, Managing Director’s message, FY2025 annual report [2]

book_paragraphs: You should model the sales cycle as a chain of gates. A public award creates a defined obligation, but it does not automatically mean a system is deployed, accepted, invoiced or collected. The APSSDC and Higher Education disclosures name buyers and scopes that include design, development, integration, deployment and maintenance. The accounting policy then shows multiple commercial forms: time-and-material, fixed-price, milestone, subscription and managed service. Each format transfers risk differently. The project’s value becomes durable only when RNIT delivers, earns acceptance, bills, collects and renews at a cost that leaves cash. [1] [5] [6]

The auditor’s key-audit-matter section maps the judgments that matter. It lists performance obligations, control transfer, stage of completion, unbilled revenue, customer acceptance and project completion. The audit team says it reviewed contracts, statements of work, timesheets, milestone confirmations and acceptance evidence. This is not an adverse finding: the auditor issued an unmodified opinion. It is a useful map for future monitoring. Ask whether contract assets grow faster than sales, whether aged receivables resolve, and how quickly a deployed system earns sign-off. A profitable statement can still leave cash tied up while milestones are pending. [1]

The ₹100 bridge converts audited FY2026 figures into comparable proportions. Revenue was ₹51.4988 crore; employee cost ₹7.9529 crore; combined operating consultancy and other expenses ₹22.8649 crore; depreciation and amortization ₹4.0016 crore; finance cost ₹0.8495 crore; other income ₹0.7803 crore; and tax ₹4.5929 crore. The resulting PAT was ₹12.0173 crore. This translates to approximately ₹23.34 PAT per ₹100 revenue. It is not proof that the same economics will repeat; the company is still early after restructuring and its cost mix includes substantial consultancy. [1]

Cash-flow math changes the interpretation. CFO was ₹11.2315 crore, but fixed-asset and intangible purchases were ₹18.9675 crore, leaving CFO less capex negative ₹7.736 crore. Other financial assets also absorbed ₹18.1094 crore in investing activities. The reported CFO reconciliation includes positive borrowing and tax-liability adjustments, while receivables and other current assets consumed cash. So an accounting profit can coexist with a funding requirement. In H1 FY2027, PAT remained positive while CFO turned negative, receivables rose and cash declined. Keep audited full-year and interim half-year data separate rather than annualizing or combining them. [1] [3]

The receivable balance is part of the product economics. At FY2026 year-end, trade receivables were ₹20.63 crore and contract assets ₹5.15 crore; at September 2026 receivables rose to ₹30.85 crore. Some growth may reflect new work or milestone timing, but the public filings do not give a project-level bridge. Your monitorable items are ageing, post-period collections, unbilled balances, acceptance lag and customer concentration. The auditor’s emphasis on milestone evidence makes these more than generic working-capital ratios. A growing order base without collection evidence can raise revenue while straining the balance sheet. [1] [3]

A SaaS component could improve the cycle if products renew, billing is standardized and delivery is reusable. Management says SaaS and O&M supported results, and accounting policies recognize subscriptions and managed services. But no recurring-revenue percentage, ARR, churn, renewal cohort or billing terms are reported. Do not assume annual prepayment or usage-based fees just because a product is cloud-native. Ask how much revenue renews without a new tender, what support effort is included and whether Faceify deployments share code. If the answers are absent, treat SaaS as a strategic option, not an established stabilizer. [1] [2] [9]

Security is part of delivery. A system may connect mobile capture, biometric templates, customer databases, APIs, cloud services and third-party components. RNIT says responsible AI and security are priorities, but filings do not show deployment-specific retention, encryption, hosting, subprocessors or incident response. A contract does not by itself prove that controls are adequate, and absence of detail is not proof of failure. The diligence standard is operational evidence: role allocation, lawful purpose, access controls, deletion, audit logs and independent testing. [1] [2]

The cost profile also requires attention. FY2026 consultancy charges were ₹14.60 crore, versus ₹7.95 crore employee-benefit expense, with 76 employees reported at year-end. The company does not specify all work included in consultancy, so do not label it all outsourced engineering. Still, future revenue growth must be read against people and third-party service costs. The key question is whether a deployment produces reusable code and renewals without proportional consultant-days. That is the difference between a software-enabled services company and a scalable software platform. [1]

Follow each project from award to bank receipt. Award size, planned users and management confidence are early signals; deployment, acceptance, invoice, collection and renewal are stronger ones. FY2026 profit improved, but capex exceeded CFO and H1 FY2027 cash conversion weakened. Your assessment should remain open: a large government project can validate capability, while a durable business must deliver securely, document acceptance and collect efficiently. [1] [3] [5] [6]

For each public engagement, ask for evidence at each stage: signed scope, performance obligations, deployment, acceptance certificate, invoice, collection and renewal. The auditor’s FY2026 procedures show RNIT itself recognizes contracts, timesheets, milestones and customer acceptance as relevant evidence. Those same milestones should structure your analysis. The company has identified buyers and projects, but public notices do not establish the complete commercial chain. [1] [5] [6]

A project-led model can be healthy if milestone discipline is strong and delivery costs are controlled. It can still consume cash because employees and consultants are paid before a buyer accepts or pays. FY2026 showed positive PAT but capex above CFO; H1 FY2027 showed negative CFO and larger receivables. This is why acceptance and billing are part of the product’s economics. The best evidence would connect contract scope, recognized revenue, receivable ageing and cash collected for named programs. [1] [3]

The contract formats also affect cash risk in different ways. Time-and-material work can bill effort but depends on records and customer approval. Fixed-price work places cost-overrun exposure on the supplier. Milestone contracts can defer invoices until delivery gates are accepted. Subscriptions may be more regular, but only if customers renew and usage costs are controlled. RNIT discloses all these forms in its accounting policy, not their proportions. Your model should therefore avoid one assumed cash-conversion cycle for every product line. [1]

The NIA award is useful because it exposes a price mechanism without disclosing a tariff. APSSDC’s 22 September notice says charging is per minute per user and payments depend on actual usage and satisfactory delivery. The project is classified Tier 7, which means above ₹25 crore under the company’s threshold schedule, but it is not a guaranteed payment of that amount. A high authorized ceiling can sit beside low realized usage. Ask for interview sessions, minutes consumed, acceptance, invoices and cash received before using the tier as revenue. [43]

The attendance contracts have a different billing unit. The Andhra Pradesh Higher Education SLA bills on processed attendance authentications and covers about 3,900 institutions and 1.3 million users for two years. Telangana’s rate contract names around one million users across institutions for three years. Neither filing publishes the price per authentication or active-user count. A broad user scope could lower customer-acquisition cost if a state deployment is reused; a one-off build could instead concentrate support effort and collection risk. The accounts do not yet identify which result is more common. [6] [11]

The best future unit-economics disclosure would reconcile each of these formats. For attendance, report paid authentications and cost per thousand checks; for NIA, active interview minutes, model/hosting costs and completed sessions; for fixed or milestone modules, disclose contract asset movement and the time from acceptance to collection. Keep the ₹100 audited waterfall as the aggregate reference while those data remain unavailable. That lets you test reuse without inventing prices or assuming all deployed users pay. [1] [3] [6] [43]

The November 2025 Telangana Social Welfare project is a useful historical illustration of usage-based SaaS: its scope covered daily attendance for about 1,70,000 students across 268 institutions, with a two-week go-live target and consideration varying with identifications. It shows how a contract can define a service unit without disclosing the rate. Do not annualize the covered population into revenue, and do not combine it with the later TGTS order unless the company provides a customer-level reconciliation. [44]

The NIA order helps distinguish award size from cash economics. The company’s Tier 7 classification is above ₹25 crore inclusive of GST, but payment is by minute and user after actual usage and satisfactory delivery. The deployment schedule is 15 working days subject to dependencies; the service period is five years from signing. The work order creates a possibility of scale, not a fixed annual subscription. Ask whether service costs, language support, inference costs and human escalation grow in proportion to billable minutes. [43]

A contract’s distribution path continues after signature. APSSDC selected RNIT as L1 through an open competitive process, and the later NoA defines a specific scope. The Higher Education SLA names the Commissionerate as the buyer; TGTS is the Telangana state undertaking managing the rate-contract orders. The filings do not identify every integrator, reseller, cloud vendor or procurement intermediary. That absence matters because channel commissions and third-party components can affect reported gross versus net revenue and project margins. [1] [5] [6] [11]

book_callouts.title: NARRATOR'S REFLECTION — follow the invoice to the bank
book_callouts.text: A deployment is not cash, and recognized revenue is not yet collected cash. Follow acceptance, billing, collections and renewal in sequence.
